_work.title: Thomas Norton — Ordinal of Alchemy (c. 1477): Manuscripts and 1652 Printed Plates
_work.blurb: The Ordinal of Alchemy (Ordinal of Alchimy) composed by the Bristol alchemist Thomas Norton c. 1477, the most important verse treatise on alchemy in Middle English. Written in rhyming couplets, the Ordinal describes the philosophical and practical stages of the Great Work through seven chapters, from the election of the alchemist to the perfection of the Stone. The work survives in seventeen manuscripts and was first printed with engraved plates in Elias Ashmole's Theatrum Chemicum Britannicum (1652).

entries.title: Norton's Master Instructs a Pupil — BL Add MS 10302 Illumination
entries.commons_file: File:Norton Ordinal of Alchemy master pupil.jpg
entries.summary: Illumination from British Library Add MS 10302 (c. 1500–1530), one of the earliest and most richly illustrated manuscript witnesses of Thomas Norton's Ordinal of Alchemy. Depicts the alchemical master instructing a pupil, illustrating Norton's insistence on legitimate transmission: the art must be learned from a true adept, not from books alone. The pupil's worthiness — measured in patience, secrecy, and philosophical preparation — is a major theme of Chapter I.

entries.title: Alchemical Preparation Stage — BL Add MS 10302 Illumination
entries.summary: Illumination from BL Add MS 10302 depicting an early preparatory stage of the Great Work as described in Norton's Ordinal. Likely corresponds to chapters II–III, covering the election of proper materials and the initial calcination or dissolution. Norton's careful attention to practical procedure — he was active in Bristol and claimed experimental success — gives these manuscript images a grounding in real laboratory culture.

entries.title: Portrait of Thomas Norton — BL Add MS 10302 Frontispiece
entries.commons_file: File:Thomas Norton alchemist portrait BL Add 10302.jpg
entries.summary: Frontispiece portrait of Thomas Norton from BL Add MS 10302. Norton (c. 1433–c. 1513/14) was a member of Parliament for Bristol and a gentleman alchemist who composed the Ordinal c. 1477. He claimed to have achieved the Great Work under the tutelage of George Ripley, though his manuscript of the Stone was allegedly stolen by the servant of his rival, the Duchess of Clarence. This rare author portrait gives a face to the most significant English alchemical poet.

entries.title: Theatrum Chemicum Britannicum — Norton's Ordinal Fig. 1 (1652 Engraving)
entries.summary: Figure 1 of the five engraved plates published in Elias Ashmole's Theatrum Chemicum Britannicum (London, 1652), the first printed edition of Thomas Norton's Ordinal of Alchemy. Ashmole's edition included five full-page engravings illustrating the Great Work. These are the only authoritative printed images of the Ordinal's content and were standard reference illustrations for 17th-century English alchemists.

entries.title: Theatrum Chemicum Britannicum — Norton's Ordinal Fig. 2 (1652 Engraving)
entries.summary: Figure 2 of the five engraved plates from Elias Ashmole's Theatrum Chemicum Britannicum (1652) for Norton's Ordinal of Alchemy. Likely depicts an intermediate stage of the Work, possibly the separation or conjunction phase described in chapters III–IV of the Ordinal.

entries.title: Theatrum Chemicum Britannicum — Norton's Ordinal Fig. 3 (1652 Engraving)
entries.summary: Figure 3 of the five engraved plates from Elias Ashmole's Theatrum Chemicum Britannicum (1652) for Norton's Ordinal of Alchemy. Mid-sequence plate, probably depicting putrefaction (nigredo) or albedo stages as described in chapters IV–V.

entries.title: Theatrum Chemicum Britannicum — Norton's Ordinal Fig. 4 (1652 Engraving)
entries.summary: Figure 4 of the five engraved plates from Elias Ashmole's Theatrum Chemicum Britannicum (1652) for Norton's Ordinal of Alchemy. Later stage in the Great Work sequence, likely depicting multiplication or the reddening stage (rubedo) as described in chapters V–VI.

entries.title: Theatrum Chemicum Britannicum — Norton's Ordinal Fig. 5: Projection (1652 Engraving)
entries.summary: Figure 5 — the concluding plate from Elias Ashmole's Theatrum Chemicum Britannicum (1652) for Norton's Ordinal of Alchemy. Depicts the culminating act of projection — the casting of the Stone upon base metals to transmute them into gold. The Ordinal's seventh and final chapter treats projection at length, describing the Stone's power of multiplication: a single grain projected upon a thousand times its weight in common metal achieves perfect transmutation.

entries.title: Ordinal of Alchemy — Ferguson MS 191, Glasgow University Library
entries.summary: Page from Ferguson MS 191, Glasgow University Library, one of the important manuscript witnesses of Thomas Norton's Ordinal of Alchemy. Ferguson 191 was part of the collection of bibliographer John Ferguson (1838–1916), professor of chemistry at Glasgow, whose Bibliotheca Chemica (1906) remains the standard reference for alchemical bibliography. This manuscript preserves an early textual and visual tradition of the Ordinal independent of the BL Add MS 10302 branch.

entries.title: Alchemical Apparatus for the Ordinal — Science History Institute DPLA Image
entries.summary: Image from a manuscript copy of Thomas Norton's Ordinal of Alchemy, held at the Science History Institute (formerly Chemical Heritage Foundation), Philadelphia, and available via the DPLA. Depicts alchemical apparatus relevant to the Ordinal's discussion of the proper vessels, fires, and instruments for the Work. The Science History Institute holds the world's most comprehensive collection of chemical and alchemical primary sources.

entries.title: Coronation Allegory from Norton's Ordinal — Science History Institute DPLA Image
entries.summary: Coronation allegory from a Science History Institute manuscript copy of Norton's Ordinal of Alchemy (via DPLA). The coronation motif — king and queen crowned in the alchemical vessel — represents the coniunctio of sulphur and mercury, the philosophical marriage that produces the Stone. This motif links the Ordinal iconographically to the Crowning of Nature (Coronatio Naturae) tradition and to the broader tradition of the alchemical royal wedding.

entries.title: Chapter Diagram — Seven Chapters of the Ordinal, Science History Institute
entries.summary: Diagrammatic page from a Science History Institute manuscript of Norton's Ordinal of Alchemy illustrating the structure of the seven chapters. Norton organized the Ordinal as seven books (Tractatus): Election of the Alchemist, Election of Materials, The Work, Fire, Vessels, Colours of the Work, and Projection. Each chapter was accompanied by illustrative diagrams in the richer manuscript copies, making this one of the more systematically illustrated alchemical texts in the English tradition.

entries.title: Thomas Norton — Full Frontispiece with Motto, from Theatrum Chemicum Britannicum
entries.summary: Full frontispiece engraving for Norton's Ordinal of Alchemy from Elias Ashmole's Theatrum Chemicum Britannicum (London, 1652). Shows Norton's name and motto alongside the opening emblematic imagery of the Ordinal. Ashmole's edition was produced in response to the Puritan hostility to alchemical learning and is the most important English anthology of alchemical verse, preserving works by Ripley, Chaucer, Lydgate, and others alongside Norton.
